questions.q: Which position is described as 'pro-choice' in the abortion debate?
options: The view that doctors should decide for everyone
The view that all life begins at birth only
The view that a woman should have the right to choose whether to continue a pregnancy
The view that abortion should never be allowed
questions.explain: The pro-choice position emphasises a woman's right to decide about her own pregnancy.

questions.q: What does 'celibacy' mean in a religious context?
options: Abstaining from marriage and sexual relations, often for religious devotion
Having many marriages
Rejecting all religious belief
Marrying as young as possible
questions.explain: Celibacy is the choice to abstain from marriage and sexual activity, often to focus on religious service.

options: A form of religious pilgrimage
A religious ceremony of marriage
Living together as a couple without being married
A vow of lifelong celibacy
questions.explain: Cohabitation means a couple living together in a sexual relationship without being legally married.

questions.q: What does the term 'sanctity of life' mean?
options: That life is sacred and God-given, and should be respected
That only human achievement matters
That life is purely a matter of chance
That life has no special value
questions.explain: Sanctity of life is the belief that life is holy, God-given and deserving of special respect.

options: The painless ending of a life to relieve suffering
A funeral ceremony
A medical examination
A type of fertility treatment
questions.explain: Euthanasia refers to deliberately ending a life, usually to relieve incurable suffering.

questions.q: What does the Christian idea of 'dominion' over creation traditionally mean?
options: Humans are given responsibility and authority to care for creation
Humans must never use natural resources
Nature has authority over humans
Humans may destroy nature freely
questions.explain: Dominion is often interpreted as responsible authority and care, not the right to exploit.

questions.q: What do most traditional religious teachings say about sexual relationships?
options: They are forbidden under all circumstances
They have no moral dimension at all
They are required of everyone before marriage
They should only take place within marriage
questions.explain: Many religious traditions teach that sex is best expressed within the commitment of marriage.

questions.q: What is a common misconception about evolution and religion?
options: That Christians hold differing views on this
That the debate is genuinely complex
That accepting evolution always means rejecting God
That some believers accept both evolution and God
questions.explain: Many religious believers accept evolution as the process through which God created life, so the two need not conflict.

questions.q: Which statement reflects a religious argument used against euthanasia?
options: Only God should decide the time of death, as life is sacred
Suffering should always be maximised
Doctors must never help patients
Life has no value
questions.explain: Some believers argue that, since life is God-given, only God should decide when it ends.

questions.q: In Christian belief, the Last Judgement is when:
options: God judges people and decides their eternal destiny
The Bible was finally completed
Jesus was put on trial by Pilate
People choose their own religion
questions.explain: At the Last Judgement Christians believe God will judge all people, leading to heaven or hell.

questions.q: Which view on contraception is held by the Roman Catholic Church?
options: The Church has no teaching on the subject
Contraception is compulsory for married couples
Artificial contraception is generally opposed, with natural family planning permitted
All forms of contraception are strongly encouraged
questions.explain: Catholic teaching generally opposes artificial contraception while permitting natural methods of family planning.

questions.q: Why might some religious believers oppose certain fertility treatments?
options: Because they replace the need for families
Because they always fail
Because they may involve discarding unused embryos, raising sanctity-of-life concerns
Because they are illegal
questions.explain: Some object where embryos are destroyed, viewing this as conflicting with the sanctity of life.
